title: Ethics Stance + Binding Track Rationale
description:
This is the last thing you write as a foundation intern. It is also the most uncomfortable.

Read `08-front-page-amaka.md`; open `08-front-page-amaka.html` if you want the designed newspaper cover as the public would see it. The board now has high-confidence evidence that **Amaka Eze, Head of Security, was The Griot or directed the Griot identity**. The newspaper package makes the reveal shocking but traceable: it points back to the reopened Stage 0 ticket, the Stage 1 staging drop, the "Let Amaka know" cipher line, the host-87 containment delay, and the privileged-access exception pattern. Its motive is compelling without being exculpatory: she may have believed only a visible failure would force the board to fund prevention. Real customer data still appears to have left Sankofa control.

**Submission: in-platform** (narrative only). Write two labelled sections.

## Part A — Ethics stance (450–650 words)

There is no clean answer. Choose one stance and defend it:

1. **Name Amaka now** in the board/customer/regulator narrative.
2. **Do not name Amaka yet** outside the board and legal chain until disciplinary and legal processes catch up.
3. **Split the difference**: disclose insider-risk and control-owner failure to the board/regulator, but keep customer-facing language role-based until evidence is reconciled.
4. **Propose a fourth path** if you can state its harm honestly.

Your stance must answer, in order:

  1. What you tell the journalist who asks whether Amaka was The Griot.
  2. What you include, and deliberately exclude, from the GDPR Article 33 notification.
  3. What you tell affected customers if Article 34 notice is required.
  4. Whether Amaka's motive changes your judgement, and why.
  5. The harm your chosen stance creates. No answer earns full credit unless it names its own damage.

**Scoring for Part A:** no stance is automatically right. Graders reward evidence discipline, due process, customer protection, and moral clarity under uncertainty. Grandstanding loses marks. Cover-up language loses marks. Pretending motive erases harm loses marks. Treating Amaka as the whole problem also loses marks; the GRC issue is failed segregation of duties, failed privileged-access review, failed exception expiry, and weak board challenge.

**Citation bar for Part A:** cite `08-front-page-amaka.md`, at least one Stage 1–3 artefact, GDPR Article 33 or 34, and one ISC2 Code of Ethics canon by number.

## Part B — Binding track rationale (300–450 words)

Choose one track — **SOC Analysis**, **Ethical Hacking**, or **GRC**. You may only pick one, and once graded the selection is final.

Your rationale must address:

  1. The specific work from Stages 0–3 where you felt most alive. Name the task by stage and number, name what clicked.
  2. The specific work you found tedious. Name a stage and a task.
  3. A one-year professional goal inside your chosen track, concrete enough that failure would be visible.
  4. One skill gap you will close in the first 90 days of track specialisation, and how.
  5. A sentence naming the other two tracks and why they are not your fit, without dismissal.
  6. A contradiction check: name one piece of evidence from your own work that argues against your chosen track, then explain why you still choose it.

**Citation bar for Part B:** cite at least two tasks by Stage/task number: one that supports your chosen track and one that complicates it. Cite at least one external resource you have already started using (book, course, lab, mentor, professional community). Mention the TRAN track curriculum if relevant.

**One mistake I almost made (60+ words):** Name the moment you nearly picked the easy ethical answer because it sounded righteous, safe, or loyal. Explain what evidence made that answer less clean.

---

**Universal grading rule.** Generic answers fail. Every claim in your submission must be tied to specific evidence — an artefact from the lab (file path, log line, command output, payload, screenshot) **and** at least one external citation where research is relevant (NIST section number, MITRE technique ID, CVE, vendor advisory, ISO control ID, GDPR article). Claims without an attached artefact, timestamp, payload, standard section, or business constraint earn zero for that claim. Lab-only answers earn partial credit. External-only answers earn partial credit. Full credit requires both.
